input: Prepare me for a meeting with Monday.com (monday.com)

what_they_do.value: monday.com is the AI workspace where people lead and agents act, turning strategy into execution at scale, trusted by nearly 250,000 customers worldwide.

priorities.priority: Becoming an AI-first company built around agents, AI credits and monday vibe
priorities.evidence: The co-CEOs say the business is 'undergoing a fundamental evolution' toward AI-first. AI ARR reached $36M in Q3 2026, made up of AI credits, agents and vibe. monday agents passed 6M interactions in under two quarters.

priorities.priority: Moving up-market to enterprise and selling multiple products
priorities.evidence: Paid customers above $100K ARR grew 33% to 2,127, and those above $500K grew 58% to 123 (as of Q3 2026). 41% of $50K+ accounts use more than one product, up from 29%. Roy Mann called the up-market move a 'natural step forward.' Marketing spend is shifting toward events, field marketing and sales headcount.

priorities.priority: Hybrid pricing: seats plus usage-based AI credits
priorities.evidence: Eran Zinman said at the Elevate 2026 investor Q&A: 'It's no longer just a seats model, it's a hybrid model.' One credit system covers vibe, agents, AI columns and AI workflows. Over 30% of $50K+ ARR accounts pay for AI credits.

priorities.priority: monday Frontier: forward-deployed engineers and managed services to drive enterprise AI deployment
priorities.evidence: Frontier was announced at Elevate 2026. It helps enterprises find where AI adds value, deploy it and manage the organizational change, and will scale through 2027 for mid-market and enterprise customers. Management said about $100M of restructuring savings will go back into AI, employee retention and Frontier.

priorities.priority: An open platform for third-party agents through APIs and MCP
priorities.evidence: monday.com says it is open to third-party agents through APIs and MCP. It reported over 75M MCP requests, with no plan to charge for them beyond existing usage fees.

challenges.challenge: Growth is slowing, retention is falling, and the stock dropped after guidance
challenges.evidence: Q4 2026 revenue guidance is $380M–$382M (about 14% YoY growth); the midpoint of $381M was below the $385.7M consensus. NDR was 108%, versus 113% the prior quarter. Shares fell after the Q3 report and were down 42.7% YTD at $82.14 (as of 2026-11-09). The CFO said stability is 'a few quarters' away, likely through 2027.

challenges.challenge: Disruption from the 20% layoff and restructuring
challenges.evidence: On July 22, 2026 the company started a restructuring plan to cut about 20% of its workforce (about 620 roles), with expected net charges of $45–55M. Headcount fell by 690 to 2,479 in Q3. CRO Casey George said the disruption 'lingered candidly a little longer than we thought.'

challenges.challenge: Unstable top of funnel and weaker SMB business as discovery moves to AI channels
challenges.evidence: Roy Mann said discovery is moving away from traditional search toward AI-driven channels and MCP. SMB additions fell and logo churn rose, which management says is 'by design.' A test that put about 25% of marketing budget into agent-focused acquisition 'didn't convert as much as we wished.' Enterprise buyers are also more deliberate and sales cycles are longer.

challenges.challenge: Pressure across SaaS from investor fears that AI agents and vibe coding will displace seat-based tools
challenges.evidence: The layoffs came during a broad SaaS selloff driven by fear of AI agents and vibe coding. As of 2026-07-22 the stock had lost more than half its value in 2026, and market cap was about $3B. Wix and Atlassian made similar cuts.

recent_changes.headline: Q3 2026: revenue of $377.5M (+19%) and a record non-GAAP operating margin of 24%, with weaker Q4 guidance
recent_changes.summary: AI ARR reached $36M and RPO was $946M (+27%). The company has bought back $735M of stock year to date. Q4 guidance implies about 14% growth. Headcount is down 690 quarter over quarter after the restructuring.

recent_changes.headline: monday Frontier unveiled at the Elevate 2026 investor Q&A
recent_changes.summary: Frontier is a managed services and deployment engineering group for enterprise AI rollouts. At the same Q&A the company also discussed hybrid seat-plus-credit pricing, a multi-product strategy (work management, CRM, service, dev) and Harmony, its voice-AI product. Mann said about 30% of R&D code is now written by AI.

recent_changes.headline: Elevate '26 user conference at the Javits Center, NYC (Oct 28–29)
recent_changes.summary: The conference focused on attendees building AI agents. It also launched The Done Awards, monday.com's first customer awards program, and featured 40+ live AI demos.

key_people.name: Roy Mann
key_people.title: Co-Founder & Co-CEO
key_people.recent: On the Q3 call (2026-11-09) he described a shift from 'managing work to doing the work with people and AI agents operating together.' He also flagged that discovery is moving to AI channels and MCP.

key_people.name: Eran Zinman
key_people.title: Co-Founder & Co-CEO
key_people.recent: He led the Frontier launch and the move to hybrid pricing. He said the transformation will 'continue into 2027' and pointed to longer enterprise sales cycles.

key_people.name: Eliran Glazer
key_people.title: Chief Financial Officer
key_people.recent: He said the slowdown 'reflects a moment transition, not a change in direction.' About $100M of savings will be reinvested in AI and Frontier. AI is automating repetitive finance work.

key_people.name: Casey George
key_people.title: Chief Revenue Officer
key_people.recent: He blamed Q3 softness on longer sales cycles, disruption from the layoffs and the up-market shift, saying Q3 'is not fun for any sales organization.'

talking_points: Discovery is moving from search to AI channels and MCP, and the agent-focused acquisition test underperformed. How are you rebuilding top-of-funnel and buyer-intent visibility, and what data do you have on where prospects find you now?

With Frontier scaling through 2027 and up-market deals taking longer, what would help your deployment engineers and sales team find and qualify the enterprise accounts most likely to expand AI credit usage?

NDR fell to 108% and the restructuring cut about 20% of staff. Where are you still investing (AI, Frontier, sales headcount), and which tools or data are now expected to replace work that people used to do?
missing_fields: Detailed Frontier launch date (the source gives only the article date, 2026-10-28)
Analyst downgrade details (TD Cowen, 2026-11-03) were seen in search results only, not on a page I opened, so they are left out
